Page gutters and content padding use clamp(); the workspace and
organization lists wrap their rows and hide the column header below 720px;
the filter popover and project select cap at the viewport width; below
Ant's md breakpoint the sidebar becomes a fixed overlay drawer with a
backdrop, closed on navigation, leaving the stored desktop collapse

  screen: the header actions and the filter's select row wrap.
- Replace antd's zero-width span trigger with a real button
  (aria-expanded, aria-controls) and leave a row for it, so it no longer
  covers the breadcrumb. The drawer closes on Escape and returns focus
  to the trigger, moves focus into the drawer when it opens, closes when

  links are out of the tab order.
- Use one breakpoint (below antd's md, 768px) for the drawer, the page
  header and the organization list. Workspace rows switch layout on the
  list's own width (container query), so they also wrap when an expanded
  sidebar leaves too little room at 1280px, where the name column used
  to collapse to nothing; the source column now gives way first.

  change, re-selecting the current page, and the stored desktop
  preference surviving a narrow round trip.

commits.author: Jake Groves
commits.message:
fix(executor): explicitly autowire BinaryCacheRecoveryService's two-arg constructor (#3654)

With two constructors and neither marked primary, Spring can't infer
which one to use and falls back to a no-arg constructor that doesn't
exist, failing every executor at startup (NoSuchMethodException:
BinaryCacheRecoveryService.<init>()).

Add a wiring test that resolves the real bean through an
ApplicationContextRunner, proving Spring picks the right constructor
rather than just asserting the class compiles.

feat(api,ui): add a public provider page and default imports to the latest version (#3647)

* feat(api,ui): add a public provider page and default imports to the latest version

Search results now open a provider page with a version picker that
preselects the registry's latest release, per-version facts (downloads,
source, published), a private-registry usage snippet, and an "Add to
Terrakube" confirmation. Previously the import dialog preselected
versions[0] of the registry response, which is not sorted, so an old
version (e.g. cloudflare v2.26.1 instead of 5.x) was chosen by default.

- API: proxy GET /registry/v1/providers/{namespace}/{name}[/{version}]; pass
  registry 4xx answers (e.g. 404) through instead of mapping them to 500,
  which showed the UI's global API error screen.
- UI: provider cards ordered official/partner first, then by downloads;
  search tab and query kept in the URL; path params URL-encoded.
- Tests: PublicRegistryProxyServiceTest and a Playwright e2e suite (e2e/)
  covering search -> provider page -> add -> cleanup and the 404 case.

* fix(api): pass through only client errors from the public registry proxy

A registry 4xx (such as 404 for an unknown provider) is passed through
for the UI to explain. A 5xx or any other failure becomes a 502 with a
fixed body instead of echoing the exception message. Retries now happen
only on a registry 5xx or a network/IO error; a 4xx is not retried.

commits.author: pokapu
commits.message:
feat(ui): edit, show and filter key/value workspace tags (#3649)

* test(api): cover key/value workspace tags over the Elide APIs

Give the demo organization two keys that carry a value (env, team) next to the
existing key-only tags, so the UI and the Terraform `cloud` block have
something to work with.

WorkspaceTagTests exercises what the UI relies on: values round trip over
JSON:API (including the explicit null of a key-only tag), and Elide matches one
key/value pair against the same binding row while an AND of two pairs
collapses into a single join alias and can never match - which is why the UI
resolves and intersects ids instead. Who may change tags is covered by
WorkspaceTagPermissionTests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(ui): set, show and filter workspace tags by value

Tags carry a value now, so the workspace UI stops treating them as bare keys.

Editing
- The workspace page lists its tags as chips, with an "Edit tags" button for
  those who may manage the workspace. The sidebar column is too narrow for a
  key and a value input side by side, so the editor opens in a modal.
- The modal edits a copy of the tags as `key = value` rows. Save sends the
  removals, value changes and new tags together and Cancel drops them. A key
  that is empty or listed twice is refused before anything is sent. The key
  of a saved tag is fixed, since a workspace holds one value per key, so
  changing it means removing the row and adding a new one.
- The API has no transaction across requests, so when part of a save fails
  the rest stays saved and the modal keeps only the failed changes, for Save
  to retry.
- Inputs stop at the column sizes: 128 characters for a key, 256 for a value.
  Organization settings call tags "tag keys", since the value now lives on
  each workspace.

Showing
- Card and table rows share WorkspaceTagChips. A chip draws the key on the
  tag's colour and the value on a pale mix of it, with full-strength text in
  both, in the light and the dark theme. Titles read `key = value`.
- Tags are ordered by key, then value. The API returns them in row order,
  which nothing fixes, so without it the tags a row shows could change
  between reads.
- The card shows every tag. The compact table has no room for chips, since
  every column other than the name has a fixed width, so a row shows a tag
  icon right after the name instead. It opens all of the chips in a popover
  on hover, on click and from the keyboard, takes no line of its own, and
  leaves as much room as it can to the name. The chips and the icon are
  stacked above the link that covers each row, or they could not be reached.

Filtering
- The tag filter applies the value that its popover has always collected,
  and keeps it when reopened. A row without a value matches any value.
- A Clear button in the popover drops just the tag filters, which only
  Clear all could do before in the card view, and the last row can be
  removed as well.
- Several tag filters are ANDed, like Terraform's own `filter[tagged]`. Elide
  cannot express that in one RSQL expression - predicates on the same
  to-many path share a join alias, so asking for two key/value pairs asks
  one binding row to carry both keys - so listWorkspacePage resolves the ids
  each filter matches in one aliased query and intersects them into an
  `id=in=(...)` predicate. That keeps paging, sorting and the facet counts on
  the server. A single filter still goes out as one query.
- The ids go back once for the page and once for each facet count, and SQL
  Server stops at 2100 parameters per statement, so an AND that matches more
  than 1000 workspaces - or a single filter that matches more than one
  10000-row page - fails with a message to narrow the filter rather than
  show a list quietly missing workspaces. A failed lookup fails the page
  too, instead of showing no workspaces. Matching on the server would lift
  both limits and is left for a follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Daniil Kivenko
commits.message:
perf(registry): parse module inputs, outputs and resources server-side (#3567)

* perf(registry): parse module inputs, outputs and resources server-side

The module details page downloaded the whole archive into the browser,
unzipped it and parsed the HCL with hcl2-parser, a 3.2 MB (753 KB gzipped)
GopherJS bundle fetched on every visit.

Add GET /terraform/modules/v1/{org}/{module}/{provider}/{version}/details
to the registry, returning variables, outputs, resources, submodules and a
submodule README from the stored archive. A small block-level scanner
extracts top-level blocks and raw attribute text without evaluating
expressions, so no HCL parser dependency is needed. The UI now makes one
request; hcl2-parser and unzipit are removed.

* fix(registry): handle HCL labels and nested templates

* fix(registry): keep heredoc relative indent and unescape strings in one pass

Indented heredocs now strip only the smallest common indent, so nested
lines in descriptions keep their structure. Quoted strings are unescaped
left to right, so an escaped backslash before n is no longer a newline,
and \t, \r, \uNNNN and \UNNNNNNNN are resolved.

* fix(registry): serve root README from details and bound module inspection

The details endpoint now returns the root module README too, so the page
makes one request and the archive is read from storage once per view.
README matching is case-insensitive.

Local storage throws StorageUnavailableException when the archive cannot
be read, like the cloud backends, instead of returning an empty zip that
would be cached as a module with no inputs.

Inspection reads at most 4 MB per file and 32 MB in total and fails with
422 beyond that, protecting the heap from huge or crafted archives.

* fix(registry): bound HCL nesting depth and reject unknown submodules in module details

- Cap block and template nesting at 64 so a crafted .tf returns 422 instead of a StackOverflowError
- Strip quotes from a heredoc marker so <<-"EOT" ends at its closing line
- Skip . and .. directories when discovering submodules
- Return 404 for a submodule that is not in the archive, which also keeps arbitrary query values out of the details cache

commits.author: Alfredo España
commits.message:
fix(api,ui): lift Elide's implicit 500-row cap on tags and add pagination to tag management (#3609) (#3635)

Elide returns at most its default page size (500) when a client does not
paginate, and Organization's read permission is evaluated in memory, so Elide
rejects explicit page[...] parameters with 'Cannot paginate tag'.
Organizations with more than 500 tags were silently truncated in both the
JSON:API relationship endpoint and GraphQL queries. Consequently, tags past
the 500 mark rendered as raw UUIDs in the workspace UI and were omitted from
the Tag Management page.

- Annotate Tag and WorkspaceTag with @Paginate(defaultPageSize = maxPageSize = 10000)
  to raise the implicit ceiling to Elide's maximum.
- Add TagPaginationTests regression test asserting retrieval of >500 tags via
  both JSON:API and GraphQL.
- Add client-side pagination to the Tag Management List in Settings/Tags.tsx.

Fixes #3609

commits.author: Jake Groves
commits.message:
fix(executor): self-heal invalid terraform/tofu binary cache archives (#3622)

* fix(executor): self-heal invalid terraform/tofu binary cache archives

A zero-byte or corrupt release archive was treated as a cache hit and never redownloaded, leaving a persistent "No such file or directory" until the pod was restarted.

ensureBinaryCached() now validates the local binary, an S3 restore, and the local archive before delegating to the library, and cleans up only the exact invalid artifact so a fresh download can proceed.

Closes #3621

* fix(executor): self-heal a missing executable bit on cached binaries

isValidExecutable() checked that a cached terraform/tofu binary was a
regular, non-empty file, but not that it was actually executable. A
zip extraction or S3 restore does not always carry the executable bit
over, which would otherwise be treated as just another invalid-cache
case - deleted and redownloaded - for a binary that was really fine.

Now sets the bit (owner-only, matching terraform-spring-boot's own
downloadTerraformBinary) when missing and re-checks before deciding
validity, so a binary missing only its executable permission is
self-healed in place instead of discarded.

Addresses review feedback from @alfespa17 on #3622.

commits.author: Daniil Kivenko
commits.message:
fix(ui): dark theme, contrast and accessibility fixes (#3570)

* fix(ui): dark theme, contrast and accessibility fixes

- Status tags derive a tinted ground and a contrast-safe text colour from
  the status hue instead of white text on a solid fill.
- The dark-theme .ant-tag override no longer forces every tag grey.
- Dark-theme links use a --tk-link token that clears 4.5:1 on graphite.
- Dark-theme block for the policy checks panel.
- Solid 2px focus rings in the structured plan output.
- aria-label on search inputs, real alt text on provider logos,
  prefers-reduced-motion handling for all animations.
- Sidebar controls use graphite tokens; the global dark link rule no
  longer applies inside the sidebar, so its menus drop !important.
- Structured plan output uses --tk-* tokens where the dark rule already
  did; redundant dark declarations removed.
- Policy rule cards use a 1px tinted border instead of a 4px left tab;
  transition: all replaced with explicit properties; dead CRA CSS removed.

* fix(ui): address review on status tag contrast, link hover and tests

Document which surfaces the tk-status-tag contrast was checked against,
and give browsers without color-mix() an explicit @supports fallback: a
var()-based value is only invalid at computed-value time, so an earlier
plain declaration would never apply.

Add --tk-link-hover so dark links keep their scheme on hover (purple
links turned blue under the terrakube scheme).

Test that status tags go through the tk-status-tag recipe instead of
Ant's color prop, and query search inputs by their new aria-labels.

Move the responsive IconSelector width to the responsive layout PR.

* chore(ui): drop local tool state committed by mistake

* fix(ui): dark tag borders, portal menu links and workspace tag text colour

Checking the branch in a browser against main turned up three issues:

- antd 6 tags default to the filled variant with a transparent border,
  so uncoloured tags (filter chips, policy set names) lost their edge in
  dark mode once the forced override was removed. Give filled tags the
  theme border; colour rules and inline colours still override it.
- The help and user menus render in a portal outside .app-sidebar, so
  the dark page link rule coloured and underlined their items.
- getDeterministicColors judged lightness from the tag id instead of the
  generated colour, and picked white text for light backgrounds.

Also assert status tags carry no inline Ant colour; antd 6 has no
ant-tag-has-color class, so the previous check could not fail.

commits.author: Jake Groves

feat: add Terraform/OpenTofu CLI login via Terrakube OAuth broker (#3599)

* feat: add configurable Terraform CLI login token duration

* fix(api): address review feedback on terraform login broker

- Stamp PAT last_used_at with a conditional UPDATE so a concurrent revoke
  is never overwritten by a stale entity save
- Claim the broker auth code with a compare-and-set status update before
  minting, so concurrent redeems of one code yield a single PAT
- Bind the login flow to the starting browser with a signed cookie set at
  /oauth/authorize and required at /oauth/callback
- Handle IdP error callbacks: fail the session and redirect the CLI with
  error=access_denied instead of a bare 400
- Restore ports [10000, 10001] on the Dex (broker disabled) discovery path
- Return the PAT id from PatService and attribute the creator there,
  removing the jti regex; drop unused touchLastUsed/renderSuccess and
  clear the login cookie after consent
- Share LOOPBACK_HOSTS between the properties and redirect validator

commits.author: Daniil Kivenko
commits.message:
fix(api): encode encrypted log-read-url values with URL-safe Base64 (#3617)

* fix(api): encode encrypted log-read-url values with URL-safe Base64

EncryptionService encoded the IV and ciphertext through a BigInteger
base36 round trip, which drops a leading 0x00 or 0xFF byte. About one
encryption in 128 produced a value that failed to decrypt with a GCM tag
mismatch, so CLI-driven runs occasionally got a log-read-url the API
could not read, and EncryptionTests was flaky.

Use URL-safe Base64 without padding. It has no "/", so the
"IV/EncryptedData" format and the two-segment log routes are unchanged.

* fix(api): fall back to legacy Base-36 decoding for encrypted values

A log-read-url handed to a Terraform CLI run before the upgrade still
carries Base-36 encoded values. If URL-safe Base64 decryption fails,
retry with the legacy encoding so those runs keep reading logs during a
rolling upgrade.

commits.author: Daniil Kivenko
commits.message:
feat(registry): deprecate and remove module and provider versions (#3596)

* feat(registry): deprecate and remove module and provider versions

Module and provider versions can now be marked deprecated (still served,
with an optional message) or removed (no longer served by the registry).

- api: deprecated/removed/deprecation_message columns on module_version and
  version; create/update/delete on versions require manage module/provider;
  the latest module version skips removed versions. Rows are kept so the
  refresh jobs do not re-import removed versions.
- registry: removed versions are hidden from the versions lists and return
  404 on download, module.zip and README; the provider versions response
  carries deprecation/removal messages in "warnings", which terraform init
  prints. Warnings are best effort and never fail the versions request.
- ui: change a version's status from the module and provider pages; status
  shown in the version picker, a banner and the usage snippet; pages open on
  the newest served version.

Closes #3579

* fix(ui): keep the message help text clear of the character counter

* feat(registry): address review on version deprecation

- Model the version state as one status column (active, deprecated,
  removed) instead of two booleans, so no combination is undefined once
  it is public API.
- Module downloads ask the API whether that exact version is removed,
  cached for 30 seconds, instead of checking the replica's cached
  version list. A version published a moment ago is no longer a 404 on
  a replica with a stale list, and a removal applies within 30 seconds.
- Provider warnings are one cached summary line listing at most five
  deprecated versions, instead of a line per version on every lookup
  and a second uncached API call per /versions request. The line needs
  no deprecation fields, so the protocols alias is gone.
- Recalculate Module.latestVersion after a module version is created,
  updated or deleted, sharing the calculation with the refresh job.
- Strip \p{Cc} and \p{Cf} (C1 controls, bidi overrides) from the
  message when it is stored, and cap it at 1024 characters with @Size
  so a longer one is a 400 instead of a database error.

The manage permissions for versions moved to their own PR (#3605).

* fix(registry): refresh the cached module version list after a removed version is requested

Terraform only downloads a removed version when a replica's cached
version list still offers it. Evict that list on the 404, so the next
run on that replica gets the list without the removed version instead
of failing until the cache expires.

commits.author: pokapu
commits.message:
Merge commit from fork

WorkspaceTag carries no permissions of its own. Elide checks the parent
workspace when a tag is added through its relationship, but nothing guards the
binding row itself, so any member of the organization can PATCH an existing
binding and point it at another tag or change its value - which is how
workspaces are selected by `terraform init` and how policies are attached.

TeamManageWorkspaceTag mirrors Workspace's own three-tier update permission
(org-wide team, project grant, workspace grant), and the entity uses it for
create, update and delete. Reading stays with the parent workspace's read
permission, because listing workspaces reads the tags of every one of them.

commits.author: Daniil Kivenko
commits.message:
fix(executor): keep terraform state and outputs out of the executor log (#3606)

* fix(executor): keep terraform state and outputs out of the executor log

After an apply, handleTerraformStateChange buffered `terraform show -json`,
`terraform state pull` and `terraform output -json` through a consumer that
also called log.info on every line. The full state was written to the pod's
stdout twice (JSON and raw), and the outputs once, including every sensitive
value in plain text. For large states this also meant hundreds of MB of log
volume per run.

The consumer now only buffers. One INFO line reports the size of each result,
and a command's output is logged as a WARN only when that command fails, since
stderr shares the buffer and then holds the error text.

Also drop the dead TerraformJob.rawState: it was set to the consumer lambda's
toString() and never read.

* fix(executor): log only stderr when show, state pull or output fails

show, state pull and output shared one buffer for stdout and stderr, so
the WARN logged on failure could contain whatever part of the state or
outputs was already printed. They now use separate buffers, as
getCurrentStateJson does, and only stderr is logged. This also keeps
Terraform warnings on stderr out of the saved state JSON.

Exclude TerraformJob.terraformOutput from toString() so logging the job
after the outputs are set can't print them.

* fix(executor): keep credentials and variables out of TerraformJob.toString()

OnlineModeServiceImpl logs the whole job at debug level, and the
generated toString() included the VCS access token, the module SSH key,
every workspace variable and environment variable (sensitive ones
included), and the policy set credentials. Exclude those fields.

commits.author: Jake Groves
commits.message:
fix(executor): stop a failed plan-summary save leaving a stale "no changes" plan (#3604)

The show -json plan summary is the authoritative structured result for a
plan step, but it was written by a single synchronous POST after the
persistence queue had already drained. One transient failure (e.g. an
object-storage timeout surfacing as a 503) left the earlier live
snapshot in place, and when that snapshot was empty the UI reported
"Your infrastructure matches the configuration" for a plan with changes.

- Publish the summary before the queue drain and, in async mode, through
  the retrying persistence queue as the step's newest final snapshot, so
  it is retried while the job is still running (context writes are
  refused once it is not).
- Track whether the plan actually streamed any -json events, and only
  publish live progress/final snapshots (and with them the noChangePlan
  marker) once it has. A plan that never streamed JSON no longer
  persists an empty change list that claims "no changes"; the summary is
  its only structured result, and the step falls back to the console
  view if even that cannot be saved.

Fixes #3602

commits.author: Jake Groves
commits.message:
fix(executor): resolve Terraform version constraints before running commands (#3603)

A workspace version such as `>= 1.3.0` or `~> 1.9` was passed straight
into TerraformProcessData. terraform-client resolves it for the download
but gates `-json` on the raw string, and any constraint compares below
0.15.2, so plan/apply/destroy silently ran without `-json`. No structured
events were produced and the structured plan view depended entirely on
the post-plan show -json summary.

Resolve the constraint to the concrete release once at the start of each
operation and store it on the job, so every process built afterwards
(init, plan/apply/destroy, show, backend override, scripts' PATH and
terraformVersion) sees a real version. If resolution fails the job keeps
its original value and behaves as before.

Fixes #3601

commits.author: Zoë
commits.message:
fix(registry): mint Azure SP/MI token before empty access token guard (#3600)

The empty access token guard added in setupCredentials() (#3371) runs
before the vcsType switch. AZURE_SP_MI never stores an access token and
mints one from the environment instead, so the guard always returned
null for it and every registry clone and tag lookup went out without
credentials.

Handle AZURE_SP_MI before the guard and add tests covering null and
empty tokens for it, plus the token-based types still returning null.

commits.message:
test(api): keep the lastJobStatus changeset in sync with JobStatus (#3566)

The 2.34.0 changeset rewrites stored ordinals to names, which is only
correct in JobStatus declaration order. Assert the changeset maps every
ordinal to the matching constant so reordering the enum without updating
